"Jurisprudence" includes legal status: permanent neutrality is a state legal status, legal obligations, obligation to not engage in war, etc. Non-aligned state has a doctrine, not a legal status. The paper states: "Permanent neutrality is a legal status consisting of well-known obligations that the armed guard cannot alter. By contrast, non-alignment is a political doctrine that does not create an obligatory legal condition; it is a principle of foreign policy, but no binding legal obligations." So the difference is that permanent neutrality is a legally protected status defined by international treaties/unilateral declarations, while non-alignment is a doctrine, not a legal status. Among options, B says that. But also option C says difference in national defence, but that says "juridically prohibited from engaging in non-violent defence". But the question states "fundamental difference in jurisprudence between a centrally neutral state and a non-aligned state." So the focus is legal status: permanent neutrality is a legal status, whereas non-alignment is a doctrine. So the answer: B.
